title: Hytale Update 7 architectural-window catalogue with native glazing and material-isolated masonry
summary: AdaptiveWindow 0.4.2 migrates 21 architectural windows from independent particle panes to native transparent model faces on released Hytale 0.7.0. Generated masonry closes each rectangular installation envelope using the selected donor material while frames and glazing remain visually independent. Existing item/state identities and multipart footprints are retained; explicit icons and dimension-prefixed English names improve creative inventory use.
problem_class: versioned asset-rendering migration with generated multipart architecture
problem_description: Correct pane rotation and displacement in the 20 generated window variants after migration to Hytale 0.7.0, add the missing donor-textured wall around non-rectangular openings without merging the frame into the wall, and make all 21 inventory items recognizable.
context: User screenshots showed particle glazing rotated or displaced from a Gothic bifora and missing masonry around the frame. The 0.4.1 generator confirmed that each opening had only a narrow adaptive reveal and that every pane was a separately transformed particle. Released 0.7.0 assets contain native transparent window faces and matching RequiresAlphaBlending block definitions.
outputs: reproducible asset generator and validation evidence
constraints: The architectural frame is not part of the adaptive wall and must retain its own texture and relief
Only masonry around and between apertures samples the selected donor material
Preserve all 21 item IDs, material-state families and native multipart footprints
Do not open, rewrite or migrate user saved worlds
Do not claim client rendering or performance from server and software-render tests
Keep the Gothic rose opening and frame circular even though its installation envelope is rectangular
known_attempts: AdaptiveWindow 0.4.1 used one fixed particle system per glazing panel and generated only a narrow donor-textured reveal around each aperture

solution_versions.description: AdaptiveWindow 0.4.2 for released Hytale 0.7.0: place glazing as native transparent quads inside each structural model; generate donor-textured masonry as separate model pieces outside the aperture union; keep every architectural frame on fixed UVs and give all 21 items explicit icons and dimension-prefixed English names.
changes: Replace every placed particle-pane attachment with a double-sided native quad whose face has transparent=true; set RequiresAlphaBlending=true and remove all legacy particle systems
Restore the original Pilot model's native glazing face rather than the 0.6.8 particle workaround
Build wall infill from the complement of the union of aperture polygons inside an odd-width, block-aligned installation envelope
Map only adaptive_wall nodes to the six donor texture slots; keep frame boxes at the fixed stone UV and glass in four shared palette sheets
Keep outer frame members deep enough to project from the masonry while inner tracery remains thin
Derive names from block envelope dimensions and English style names; retain 3x7x1_window for the original
Generate 21 transparent 128x128 item icons from the actual models and register explicit Icon paths
Preserve stable IDs, material definitions, learned aliases and all 84 prior multipart footprints
Install only the shared 0.4.2 JAR, with checksum validation and recoverable backup of 0.4.1
advantages: Pane, frame and block orientation use one model transform, eliminating independent particle offsets and rotations
Selected wall material cannot recolor the frame or glazing because their atlas regions are disjoint and validated across all states
Curved and circular windows show donor masonry outside their aperture without rectangular glass corners
No saved-world conversion and no runtime asset registration
Explicit names and silhouettes make the creative inventory catalogue usable
disadvantages: The 0.7.0 pack decodes about 172.78 MiB of RGBA texture pixels; client GPU/FPS impact is unmeasured
A rectangular installation envelope means the rose is surrounded by adaptive masonry even though its visible frame and opening are circular
Software inspection and dedicated-server validation do not certify final client transparency, lighting or aesthetics
The combined block still has one break lifecycle rather than independently breakable wall, frame and panes

solution_versions.description: Adaptive Window 0.4.7-rc.2 on Hytale 0.7.4: client-compatible, single-direction architectural transitions for 21 saved-compatible windows, with frame-supported extension where surrounding masonry is too narrow.
changes: Serialize model UV offsets and quad dimensions as integers; preserve precise geometry with stretch
Bake fringe face orientation into the mesh and leave only yaw on the block entity so pivot order cannot displace the vertical anchor
Choose one transition direction per contact: surrounding cube to window first, stable material order for window pairs
Allow transition overlap onto actual opaque frame boxes when wall space is insufficient; exclude glazing, empty space and unsupported oblique faces
Preserve all 21 window IDs, saved material states, original frame and glass geometries; source donor samples locally rather than embedding donor pixels in the public JAR
advantages: User reports the installed rc.2 transition appearance works perfectly in the real client on 2026-10-25
Client model parser contract and serialized pose are checked over the actual generated assets
Existing worlds retain their window IDs, geometry and saved materials
disadvantages: 35,665 render-only helper block types increase metadata and parsing cost, not captured by image pixel budget
No measured FPS or low-power second-PC result; unsupported oblique frame faces are omitted
Visual approval does not establish asset redistribution rights or public-release readiness
